month: # 1. One row per (month provider model workload) tuple. If you cannot split by workload yet leave it as 'unattributed' and treat the size of that row as finding #1.
# 2. cost_per_unit_usd = provider_cost_usd / units_delivered. This is the number to track over time. Total spend rises with growth and tells you nothing on its own.

# 3. units_delivered is deliberately not requests. Work that was billed but did not produce a result (capped agent loops retried calls abandoned sessions) belongs in the cost column and not in the units column.
# 4. quality_metric is mandatory. A cost_per_unit that fell while quality also fell is not a saving and the sheet must be able to show that.
# 5. Keep reasoning_tokens separate from output_tokens. They bill as output on most providers but they scale with prompt design rather than response length so mixing them hides the lever.
# 6. Rebuild from raw provider invoices not from a dashboard. A baseline you cannot reconcile to an invoice is not a baseline.
